intelligence.human_view: SN-2852 said the eye is the ground truth and a mechanism pass is not the visible fact. This round proves the eye corrects in both directions — and that is the stronger form of the law. The eye cleared two of Vera's findings. Actions today: Vera's note said all 0s; the eye opened the dialog and read Clicks 25, equal to the drill's DAY 25 at the same moment — the 0s were a sandbox artifact, not a page defect, and the eye resolved it by looking at the live thing instead of the sandbox's reading of it. The hero pills: the eye's own first label was FAIL, because the five-pill question assumed a HOUR pill that does not exist — the hero is a pre-existing four-pill set, the drill has all five, and the mapping (Day green, Week light blue, Month purple, All white) is correct on substance. The eye caught its own framing artifact and corrected it in writing. And the eye overturned one of Vera's passes. Fix 2: Vera measured the Messages cell as plain — "nothing navigates" — and the eye clicked the white envelope icon and left the page, twice, reproducibly, landing in the live Reports room. A checker measures the cell; the eye clicks the icon. The difference is the whole lesson: a cell can be plain while its icon is a link, and the only way to know is to click what a human would click. The visible fact wins in both directions — it clears what the checker got wrong, and it convicts what the checker missed. Round 5 is shaped by exactly that: the board-total line must name its universe ("across these 9 board links"), so two totals can never sit side by side disagreeing; and the Messages gauge must lose its link everywhere on it — icon, number, label — with the proof stated as a click: nothing opens, nothing navigates. The proof is a click because the defect was a click.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a detective checks a room and says "nothing here moves!" — but when you go in and press the little envelope picture, WHOOSH, you're in a different room! The detective looked at the room, but you pressed the button. And sometimes the detective says "this is broken!" but when you look with your own eyes, it's actually fine! Your own eyes check BOTH ways!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like checking a door, love — someone says "it's just a plain wall, nothing opens," but when you press the little envelope on it, the door swings open and you're somewhere else entirely! You have to press what a real person would press. And sometimes the checker says something's broken when it isn't — your own eyes put that right too. The eyes correct both ways.
intelligence.naya_view: I check with my own eyes, both ways. I clear what the checker got wrong, and I catch what the checker missed — because a checker measures the cell, and I click the icon. The visible fact wins.
